title: instrument channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.instrument.channel.v1). Replaces legacy `securities/list`, `setup/markets`+`get_assign`+`set_assign`, and `account/get_catalog`+`get_instrument`+`resolve_instrument` for clients that negotiated this capability; legacy stays available as fallback. `list`/`get`/`resolve`/`detail` are open to any authenticated caller (unlike legacy `securities/list`, which allowed anonymous access — that is not carried over). `pool`/`apply` are manager-only: `pool` browses candidate instruments (from the daily MOEX/ISS refresh or a connector's own broker.get_catalog) that are not yet part of the curated set; `apply` is the sole write — a bulk, all-or-nothing replace of the whole curated set (items + groups + assets), never a per-item mutation. `resolve` keeps the pre-flight semantics of legacy `account/resolve_instrument` (compiles a tradeplan draft and asks the target BF to resolve it) but returns the canonical instrument shape instead of an untyped proxy blob. `detail` is a lighter sibling of `resolve` for the tradeplan editor: given just `bf_id`+`ticker` for an already-catalogued instrument, it fetches live broker-side trading params (margin, tradable/longable/shortable) without compiling a draft — no new AFB<->BF wire message, it drives the same `broker.resolve_instrument` mechanism as `resolve` against a minimal synthetic venue triplet. See AFB/docs/ENTITY_WS_PROTOCOL.md. Federated-catalog phase 2 adds `catalog`/`commit`/`user`, which express the catalog as arbitrary, freely overlapping SETS (see catalogSetEntry/setMembership) instead of the single-parent group tree, plus an independent futures-series axis (catalogSeries) in place of `asset`: `catalog` is the full snapshot in that form for any authenticated caller, `commit` is the manager-only, CAS-guarded delta write against a `base_revision` (a stale revision comes back as `conflict` with the current one in errorResponse.details), and `user` is the personal-sets/overlay operation of phase 3 — declared here so clients can be written against the final shape, while the phase 2 backend answers it with `unsupported_action`. `list` and `apply` are deprecated by that trio: the backend keeps serving `list` for frontends that predate `catalog`, but stops serving `apply` (`unsupported_action`) — `commit` is the only write. `get`/`pool`/`resolve`/`detail` are unchanged.

catalogSet.title: The curated instrument set — items + the groups/assets they're organized into.

catalogSetEntry.title: One catalog set — an arbitrary, freely overlapping selection of instruments (phase 2 replacement for the single-parent `group`).
catalogSetEntry.description: Sets overlap by design: a listing may belong to any number of them, or to none. `set_id` is the stable identity, generated by the server and never chosen by a client; `key` is the readable slug, unique within scope+owner. The old system/global division is gone — every non-personal set is `global` and is curated by a manager; `user` sets are the personal selections of phase 3 and are the only ones carrying `owner_user_id`.

set_id.description: Stable server-generated id — the only handle memberships and edits refer to.

scope.description: `global` — manager-curated, visible to everyone; `user` — personal (phase 3). "system" is not part of this form and is never emitted.

archived.description: An archived set stays addressable (history, links) but is hidden from ordinary pickers.

owner_user_id.description: Owner of a scope="user" set; null/absent for global sets.

setMembership.title: Membership edge — this ticker is in this set, at this position.
setMembership.description: The authoritative record of membership in the phase 2 form: nothing else (least of all instrument.v1's legacy `group`) decides which sets a listing belongs to.

ticker.description: Canonical wire ticker, exactly as in instrument.v1.json — case-sensitive, never normalized.

sort_order.description: Position of this member inside its set.

catalogSeries.title: A futures series (map value, keyed by series_code) — the phase 2 successor of `asset`.
catalogSeries.description: An axis of its own, independent of sets: it groups the successive expirations of one futures contract and is unaffected by set membership.

underlying_ticker.description: Canonical ticker of the underlying instrument, when the series has one.

userState.title: The caller's personal catalog overlay: own sets, own memberships, hidden sets, personal ordering.
userState.description: Phase 3 payload, declared now so clients can be written against the final shape. The phase 2 backend never emits it and rejects `user` requests with `unsupported_action`.

revision.description: Revision of the PERSONAL aggregate — counted separately from catalog_revision.

sets.description: The caller's own sets — every entry has scope: "user".

memberships.description: Membership edges of the personal sets.

hidden_set_ids.description: Sets (global or personal) the caller hid from their own view.

order.description: Personal ordering of set_ids; sets not listed here follow the listed ones in their server sort_order.

listRequest.title: No filters — returns the full curated set (as legacy securities/list + setup/get_assign combined).
listRequest.description: DEPRECATED since federated-catalog phase 2 — superseded by `catalog`, which returns the same listings organized as overlapping sets plus a `catalog_revision` to commit against. Still served by the backend for frontends that predate `catalog`; the group/asset shape it answers with is the legacy projection of the set model, not its authoritative form. New clients must use `catalog`.

poolRequest.title: manager only. `exchange`/`market` both present -> a slice; both absent -> just the meta (exchanges/markets available from this source).

source.description: "moex" for the daily ISS-fed candidate pool, or a bf_id to browse that connector's own broker.get_catalog.

query.description: Optional substring filter over ticker/name. Applied server-side for source="moex" (a local, in-memory scan); a broker source ignores it today and returns the full slice — the client filters client-side, same as it already does for the curated list (see TickersService.tsx).

poolSliceResponse.title: Candidate rows, normalized into the canonical shape with group: null (not yet distributed).

applyRequest.title: manager only. Bulk replace of the whole curated set — validated and enriched (broker.get_instrument for source != moex rows missing trading params) atomically before write; never partial.
applyRequest.description: DEPRECATED since federated-catalog phase 2 and no longer served — the backend answers it with `unsupported_action`. Its whole-set replace cannot express overlapping sets and has no concurrency guard; `commit` replaces it with a CAS delta on `base_revision`. Kept in the schema only so an older frontend's request still parses into a typed error instead of `invalid_schema`.

applyResponse.title: The authoritative saved set, after enrichment.

catalogRequest.title: Full catalog snapshot in the set-based phase 2 form — open to any authenticated caller. No filters, no paging.

catalogResponse.title: The authoritative snapshot: listings, sets, membership edges and futures series, stamped with the revision to commit against.
catalogResponse.description: `memberships` is the only authoritative statement of which sets a listing belongs to. The `group` field inside `items[]` is a legacy leftover carried for compatibility with clients still on `list` — it is NOT read in this form and must not be interpreted as membership. A listing that appears in `items` with no membership edge at all is normal (nothing forces a listing into a set) and stays visible to a manager. `series` is the independent futures-series axis, replacing the old `assets` map.

catalog_revision.description: Revision of the global catalog this snapshot was taken at — send it back as commitRequest.base_revision.

setUpsert.title: Create-or-update of one set inside a commit. `set_id` absent -> create (the server generates both set_id and key).

set_id.description: Existing set to update; omit to create a new one.

key.description: Requested slug; ignored on create if it collides, the server owns uniqueness within scope+owner.

membersEdit.title: Membership delta for one set. add/remove are applied first, then `order` (when present) fixes the resulting positions.

add.description: Canonical tickers to add; adding an already-present ticker is a no-op, not an error.

remove.description: Canonical tickers to drop from this set — removing the last set of a listing does not delete the listing.

order.description: The FULL member order of this set after add/remove — not a partial reshuffle.

listingArchival.title: Archive one listing (the instrument record itself, not its membership).

reason.description: Free-form note stored with the audit entry (e.g. "expired", "delisted").

seriesUpsert.title: Create-or-update of one futures series, keyed by its series_code.

commitRequest.title: manager only. The single write of the phase 2 catalog: a delta applied atomically on top of `base_revision`, never a whole-set replace.
commitRequest.description: Compare-and-set: if the server's current catalog revision differs from `base_revision` the whole commit is rejected with `conflict` and errorResponse.details.catalog_revision carries the current one — the client re-fetches `catalog`, re-applies its edits and retries. Every section is optional; an empty commit is legal (and is a cheap way to read the current revision back). All sections are applied in one transaction: sets, then remove_sets, then members, then listings/archive_listings, then series.

base_revision.description: The catalog_revision these edits were built on (CAS guard).

remove_sets.description: set_ids to delete outright (their membership edges go with them); archiving instead is a setUpsert with archived: true.

listings.description: Upsert of the instrument records themselves, by `ticker`. The element's `group` field is IGNORED here — membership is expressed only through `members`; clients send `group: null`. instrument.v1 is reused verbatim for its class gating (futures-only expiration/step_price/margin/futoi_code, `isin` for stock only), which is exactly what a listing write has to enforce.

reason.description: Operator's note for this commit — stored verbatim in catalog_audit.reason.

commitResponse.title: The full post-commit snapshot (same shape as catalogResponse), so a client never has to re-read after a successful write.
commitResponse.description: `catalog_revision` is already the new one. A rejected commit is an errorResponse instead — there is no partially-applied outcome.

applied.title: What the commit actually changed, as counts — the same summary stored in catalog_audit.summary.

userRequest.title: The caller's own personal sets and overlay — same delta shape as commit, but scoped to the caller. PHASE 3: the phase 2 backend answers `unsupported_action`.
userRequest.description: `base_revision` here is the revision of the PERSONAL aggregate (userState.revision), not the global catalog_revision — personal edits never conflict with a manager's commit. Sets created through this operation are implicitly scope: "user" and owned by the caller; a `set_id` naming a global set is rejected. An empty request is legal and just reads the current personal state back.

base_revision.description: userState.revision the edits were built on (CAS guard); a mismatch is `conflict` with details.user_revision.

sets.description: Personal sets to create or update — scope is implied, never sent.

hidden_set_ids.description: Replaces the whole hidden list, not a delta.

order.description: Replaces the whole personal ordering, not a delta.

userResponse.title: The caller's personal state after the edit — the global catalog is untouched, so no catalog_revision is returned.

user_revision.description: The new personal revision — same value as user.revision, hoisted for symmetry with catalog_revision.

resolveRequest.title: Pre-flight: compiles a tradeplan (draft or by id) into a deal and asks the target BF to resolve its instrument, without publishing.

binding.description: Broker-native locator, BF-owned shape — see broker.instrument_resolved.json.

detailRequest.title: Lightweight live broker lookup for an already-catalogued instrument — no tradeplan draft/compile involved, unlike resolve. Used while editing a tradeplan, right after a ticker+connector are picked, to preview tradability/margin before any entry/quantity condition exists.

ticker.description: Canonical ticker of an item already present in the curated catalog (see instrument/get) — not an arbitrary broker-native symbol.

detailResponse.title: Same {item, binding, broker_instrument} shape as resolveResponse — same underlying BF mechanism (broker.resolve_instrument against a minimal synthetic venue triplet), just without compiling a tradeplan/deal first.

binding.description: Broker-native locator, BF-owned shape — see broker.instrument_resolved.json.

broker_instrument.description: Broker-owned trading params, BF-owned shape (InstrumentInfo.to_broker_instrument_dict() — the same deal-publish-shared shape resolveResponse carries, not the narrower broker.instrument.json allow-list; e.g. it has no `symbol` key, that lives in `binding` instead).

errorDetails.title: Typed context for a rejected catalog/user write — chiefly the revision to rebase onto, plus which sets/tickers were at fault.
errorDetails.description: Populated on `conflict` (stale base_revision: `catalog_revision` for commit, `user_revision` for user — re-fetch, re-apply, retry) and on `validation_error` (`set_ids`/`tickers` name the offending rows). Absent for errors that carry no such context.

catalog_revision.description: The server's current global catalog revision.
